explanations.answer: They've been unfaithful to their God
explanations.explanation: Right on the money, baker. The message says Israel has played the harlot against their God. That is why the party gets shut down before it starts. Nobody wants confetti on a day like that.

explanations.answer: They just lost their king in battle
explanations.explanation: No king and no battle show up in this verse. The reason given is that Israel has played the harlot against their God. So this isn't a mourning rule, it's about faithfulness. I'd be confused too if someone canceled my cookie party and left out the reason.

explanations.answer: Their harvest came in far too late
explanations.explanation: The harvest timing never comes up here. The verse says Israel has played the harlot against their God. It does mention threshing floors, which are harvest places, but the problem is where Israel's loyalty went. A late harvest isn't the charge.

It's the other way around, friend. The verse says the threshing floor and winepress will not feed them. It also says the new wine will fail them. Hosea 9:2 is a message of empty tables, not full ones.
That's it. Hosea 9:2 says the threshing floor and winepress will not feed them, and the new wine will fail them. Those were the places food and wine came from. Now they come up empty.
Assyria it is. The verse says Ephraim will return to Egypt and eat unclean food in Assyria. Two places named, and neither one is home. Home is the land of the LORD, and they won't remain in it.
Babylon is a famous name, so I see why it came to mind. But Hosea 9:3 doesn't mention it. The verse says Assyria is where Ephraim eats unclean food. Stick to the text and it will steer you right.
Moab never comes up in this verse. Hosea 9:3 says Ephraim will return to Egypt and eat unclean food in Assyria. That's the second stop on the list. The answer is Assyria.

The message says the opposite, baker. Their bread will be for themselves, and it will not enter the house of the LORD. So nothing from that bread goes through the door. I know that's a hard line to read.
Yes. Hosea 9:4 says their bread will be for themselves and will not enter the house of the LORD. The bread stays out. The verse also says all who eat will be defiled.

Memphis, exactly. Hosea 9:6 says that even if they flee destruction, Egypt will gather them and Memphis will bury them. Running doesn't change the ending in that verse. Heavy, but that's what the text says.

Nineveh is a name you'll meet in other parts of the Bible, but it isn't in this verse. Here it says Egypt will gather them and Memphis will bury them. That's the city the message names. Check the verse and Memphis pops right out.
Tarshish doesn't appear in Hosea 9:6. The verse says Egypt will gather them and Memphis will bury them. So Memphis is the city to pick. Good guess on a good-sounding name, though.

Yes, ma'am, or sir, whichever baker this is. Hosea 9:6 says thorns will overrun their tents. It also says thistles will take over their precious silver. Whatever they were counting on gets covered in weeds.
The text says it does. Hosea 9:6 says thorns will overrun their tents. Their precious silver is taken over by thistles too. So this one is true, friend.

Fool is the word. The verse says the prophet is called a fool because of the greatness of their iniquity and hostility. The one bringing the message gets the insult. I've been called plenty myself, and mine were about flour on my hat.
I wish, baker. The verse says the opposite. The prophet is called a fool, and the inspired man insane. Hero would be a nicer thing to hear, but Hosea 9:7 doesn't say it.
Judge isn't the word the verse uses. Hosea 9:7 says the prophet is called a fool. That's what Israel's iniquity and hostility turn into. So fool fills the blank.

explanations.answer: In the house of his God
explanations.explanation: That's the shocker. Hosea 9:8 says, 'Hostility is in the house of his God!' It's the very place you'd expect it least. That's why the verse ends with an exclamation point.
A palace would be an easy guess for trouble. But Hosea 9:8 puts the hostility somewhere else. It says hostility is in the house of his God. That's what makes the line so shocking.

explanations.answer: At the gates of the city
explanations.explanation: The city gates aren't in this verse. Hosea 9:8 says hostility is in the house of his God. The line is shocking because of where it lands. The answer is the house of God.
Guilt, yes. Hosea 9:9 says He will remember their guilt and punish their sins. The verse also says they have deeply corrupted themselves. It's a serious line, so I'll just say it plainly.
Kindness would be a lovely word to find in that blank. But Hosea 9:9 says He will remember their guilt. That's what comes right before He punishes their sins. Guilt is the word.
Prayers don't come up in this verse. Hosea 9:9 says God will remember their guilt, and punish their sins. The blank wants guilt. Good news, you'll get another try on the next one.

explanations.answer: As detestable as what they loved
explanations.explanation: That's the line. Hosea 9:10 says they became 'as detestable as the thing they loved.' They went to Baal-peor and consecrated themselves to Shame. What they gave themselves to marked them.

explanations.answer: As strong as the nations around them
explanations.explanation: Strength isn't what the verse says. Hosea 9:10 says they became as detestable as the thing they loved. That happened after they went to Baal-peor and consecrated themselves to Shame. The nations' strength never comes up.

explanations.answer: As free as birds in the wilderness
explanations.explanation: Birds do fly through this passage, but not here. Hosea 9:10 says they became as detestable as the thing they loved. The wilderness in this verse is where the LORD found them like grapes. The answer is the detestable one.
True. Hosea 9:11 says Ephraim's glory will fly away like a bird, with no birth, no pregnancy, and no conception. I think this one hurts to read. It's a heavy verse, so we'll take it slow.
It's true, baker. Hosea 9:11 says Ephraim's glory will fly away like a bird, with no birth, no pregnancy, and no conception. I think this is a hard verse to sit with. It's okay to feel that.
Yes. Hosea 9:12 says, 'Yes, woe be to them when I turn away from them!' The woe comes when the LORD turns away. It's a sober line, and it's what the text says.
The verse says it. Hosea 9:12 reads, 'Yes, woe be to them when I turn away from them!' So the statement is true. It's right there at the end of the verse.
Gilgal. Hosea 9:15 says all their evil appears at Gilgal, and that there the LORD hated them. It's a strong thing to say about a place. The text points right at it.
Bethel is a name you'll find elsewhere in Scripture, but it isn't in this verse. Hosea 9:15 says all their evil appears at Gilgal. There the LORD hated them. The answer is Gilgal.
Shiloh isn't the place named here. Hosea 9:15 says all their evil appears at Gilgal. That's where the LORD says He hated them. Gilgal is the answer.

His house, baker. Hosea 9:15 says, 'I will drive them from My house for the wickedness of their deeds.' It's the same house where hostility showed up back in verse 8. The text says they get driven out.
A palace is a reasonable guess for this kind of message. But Hosea 9:15 says the LORD will drive them from His house. The wickedness of their deeds is given as the reason. The answer is His house.
Samaria doesn't show up in this verse. Hosea 9:15 says the LORD will drive them from His house for the wickedness of their deeds. That's the place the text names. The answer is His house.
The text says the opposite. Hosea 9:15 says all their leaders are rebellious. Faithful isn't the word the LORD uses. So this one is false.
False is right. Hosea 9:15 says all their leaders are rebellious. That's the opposite of faithful. A pretty clear line, which helps.
Fruit. Hosea 9:16 says their root is withered, so they cannot bear fruit. It ties back to the grapes and first figs in verse 10. A dried-up root can't make a harvest.
Thorns did show up earlier, taking over the tents in verse 6. But this verse is about a withered root. Hosea 9:16 says they cannot bear fruit. The answer is fruit.
Bark is a tree word, so I see where you were headed. But Hosea 9:16 says their root is withered, so they cannot bear fruit. The picture is about a plant that can't produce. The answer is fruit.

That's the reason the text gives. Hosea 9:17 says, 'My God will reject them because they have not obeyed Him.' It's a plain statement, and it comes at the very end of the message. Disobedience is the stated reason.
Battles aren't the reason here. Hosea 9:17 says God will reject them because they have not obeyed Him. Losing wars isn't mentioned in the verse. Obedience is the issue.
A treaty never comes up in this verse. Hosea 9:17 says God will reject them because they have not obeyed Him. That's the reason given. Not obeying is the answer.
Wanderers. Hosea 9:17 says they shall be wanderers among the nations. Back in verse 3, they were already headed for Egypt and Assyria. The message ends with no place to settle.
Rulers would be a big turn, but that isn't what the verse says. Hosea 9:17 says they shall be wanderers among the nations. Rejected by God, they don't take charge anywhere. The answer is wanderers.
Teachers is a nice word, but it isn't in this verse. Hosea 9:17 says they shall be wanderers among the nations. That's what happens after God rejects them. The answer is wanderers.
